sentences.cn: 我没有完成咒印就说出了草药名'荆棘花'，现在我书桌周围的空气在颤抖。

sentences.en: Shen Wujiu grabbed my wrist.
sentences.cn: 沈无咎抓住了我的手腕。

sentences.en: 'Hold still,' he said.
sentences.cn: '别动，'他说。

sentences.en: 'An *attack* from your own formula — breathe and complete it.'
I exhaled, traced the final stroke, and the trembling died.
sentences.cn: 我呼出一口气，描完最后一笔，颤抖消停了。

heavy:2.en: Master Qingwu placed a single jade slip on the stone table before me. I expected something small and light, but the moment my fingers closed around it my arm sank. The slip was *heavy* with decades of compressed word-energy, every formula she had ever sealed pressed into one cold surface. 'Read it slowly,' she said. 'Or it will read you.'
heavy:2.cnHint: 师尊交给我一枚玉简，它____得出乎意料，里面封存着无数咒方。
heavy:2.hook: Outside, the clouds beneath the mountain began to glow a dim, bruised violet.
heavy:2.line: 'This slip is *heavy* with every word I have sealed — do not rush it.'

sentences.en: Master Qingwu placed a single jade slip on the stone table before me.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊在石桌前放了一块玉简。

sentences.en: I expected something small and light, but the moment my fingers closed around it my arm sank.
sentences.cn: 我原本以为会很轻很小，但当我的手指合上它时，我的整条手臂都沉了下去。

sentences.en: The slip was *heavy* with decades of compressed word-energy, every formula she had ever sealed pressed into one cold surface.
'Read it slowly,' she said.
sentences.cn: '慢慢读，'她说。

sentences.en: 'Or it will read you.'
sentences.cn: '不然它会读你。'

thought:2.en: I found Xiaoxing sitting at the edge of the cliff, legs dangling above the clouds. She held a dried leaf from the word-herb 'Silvertongue' and turned it slowly. 'I had a *thought*,' she said without looking up. 'If a word can heal a wound, can it also heal a memory?' I sat beside her. Neither of us had an answer, but asking felt like the first step toward one.
thought:2.cnHint: 师妹坐在悬崖边，若有所思地问了一个关于词语力量的____。
thought:2.hook: Below us, something large moved silently through the cloud-sea.
thought:2.line: 'I had a *thought* — can a word heal a memory the way it heals a wound?'

sentences.en: I found Xiaoxing sitting at the edge of the cliff, legs dangling above the clouds.
sentences.cn: 我发现小杏坐在悬崖边，两条腿在云海上方摇晃。

sentences.en: She held a dried leaf from the word-herb 'Silvertongue' and turned it slowly.
sentences.cn: 她拿着一片干枯的'银舌'字草，慢慢转动它。

sentences.en: 'I had a *thought*,' she said without looking up.
'If a word can heal a wound, can it also heal a memory?'
sentences.cn: '如果一个字能治疗伤口，它也能治疗记忆吗？'

sentences.en: I sat beside her.
sentences.cn: 我在她身边坐下。

sentences.en: Neither of us had an answer, but asking felt like the first step toward one.
sentences.cn: 我们都没有答案，但提出这个问题感觉像是走向答案的第一步。

attract:2.en: The library at the peak was forbidden after dark, yet my lantern seemed to *attract* the sealed doors open one by one as I walked past. Master Qingwu had said certain disciples carry a resonance that wakes sleeping texts. I had not believed her until the fourth door swung wide and a warm gold light spilled out, revealing a room I had never seen on any map of the sect.
attract:2.cnHint: 我夜游藏书阁，发现自己似乎能____那些封闭的门，它们一扇扇自动开启。
attract:2.hook: From inside the gold-lit room came a voice that knew my name.
attract:2.line: 'Some disciples *attract* sleeping texts — it seems you are one of them.'

sentences.en: The library at the peak was forbidden after dark, yet my lantern seemed to *attract* the sealed doors open one by one as I walked past.
Master Qingwu had said certain disciples carry a resonance that wakes sleeping texts.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊说过，某些弟子身上带着一种共鸣，能唤醒沉睡的文献。

sentences.en: I had not believed her until the fourth door swung wide and a warm gold light spilled out, revealing a room I had never seen on any map of the sect.
sentences.cn: 直到第四扇门突然洞开，温暖的金色光芒倾泻而出，我才相信了她的话——那是一个我从未在宗门地图上见过的房间。

define:2.en: Shen Wujiu set down his brush and looked at me. 'You cannot copy a formula you do not understand,' he said. 'So *define* the word 'Veilgrass' for me — not what the scroll says, but what you feel when you speak it.' I closed my eyes. The word tasted like early fog and something older. When I described it, he nodded slowly, as if I had passed a test I had not known I was taking.
define:2.cnHint: 师兄要我不看书卷，用自己的感受来____一个草药词的含义。
define:2.hook: The candle flame turned pale green and stayed that way.
define:2.line: '*Define* 'Veilgrass' for me — not the scroll's words, but your own.'

sentences.en: Shen Wujiu set down his brush and looked at me.
sentences.cn: 沈无咎放下笔，抬眼看我。

sentences.en: 'You cannot copy a formula you do not understand,' he said.
sentences.cn: "你抄不了不理解的方子，"他说。

sentences.en: 'So *define* the word 'Veilgrass' for me — not what the scroll says, but what you feel when you speak it.'
I closed my eyes.
sentences.cn: 我闭上眼睛。

sentences.en: The word tasted like early fog and something older.
sentences.cn: 这个字尝起来像清晨的雾，还有什么更古老的东西。

sentences.en: When I described it, he nodded slowly, as if I had passed a test I had not known I was taking.
sentences.cn: 我描述出来时，他缓缓点头，好像我通过了一场我都没意识到在进行的考验。

executive:2.en: The sect's inner council met once each season, and the *executive* elder who carried out their decisions was a tall woman named only by her title: the Cloud Keeper. She arrived at my door before dawn with a sealed letter. 'The council chose you for the night watch,' she said, pressing it into my hands. 'Do not be late.' The wax seal on the letter was already cracked, as if something inside had been trying to leave.
executive:2.cnHint: 内院的____长老在天亮前来到我门前，带来了一封奇怪的封蜡信件。
executive:2.hook: The cracked seal on the letter moved — a hairline split widening in the silence.
executive:2.line: 'I am the *executive* elder — the council's will passes through my hands.'

sentences.en: The sect's inner council met once each season, and the *executive* elder who carried out their decisions was a tall woman named only by her title: the Cloud Keeper.
She arrived at my door before dawn with a sealed letter.
sentences.cn: 她在天亮前敲响我的门，手里拿着一封封好的信。

sentences.en: 'The council chose you for the night watch,' she said, pressing it into my hands.
sentences.cn: "宗主议会选了你守夜，"她说着把信塞进我手里。

sentences.en: 'Do not be late.'
sentences.cn: "别迟到。"

sentences.en: The wax seal on the letter was already cracked, as if something inside had been trying to leave.
sentences.cn: 信上的蜡封已经裂开了，像里面有什么东西在试图逃出来。

expectation:2.en: Master Qingwu reviewed my word-herb test without expression. I had studied for ten days, skipping meals, certain I would impress her. She set the paper down. 'Your results meet *expectation*,' she said. Nothing more. I felt the weight of that word — not failure, not praise, but a quiet instruction that the path ahead was still very long. Outside, the wind shifted and carried the scent of rain from below the cloud-sea.
expectation:2.cnHint: 师尊评价我的测试'符合____'，这四个字让我深感前路漫长。
expectation:2.hook: Rain from below the clouds meant a storm was rising — cloud-sea storms never gave warning.
expectation:2.line: 'Your work meets *expectation* — the path ahead remains long, disciple.'

sentences.en: Master Qingwu reviewed my word-herb test without expression.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊面无表情地看完了我的识字-草药测试。

sentences.en: I had studied for ten days, skipping meals, certain I would impress her.
sentences.cn: 我研习了十天，顾不上吃饭，确信能给她留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: She set the paper down.
sentences.cn: 她放下纸。

sentences.en: 'Your results meet *expectation*,' she said.
Nothing more.
sentences.cn: 没有更多的话。

sentences.en: I felt the weight of that word — not failure, not praise, but a quiet instruction that the path ahead was still very long.
sentences.cn: 我感受到那个词的分量——不是失败，不是表扬，而是一个无声的指示，前面的路还很长。

sentences.en: Outside, the wind shifted and carried the scent of rain from below the cloud-sea.
sentences.cn: 窗外风向转了，吹来云海下方的雨腥。

friendly:2.en: I had heard Shen Wujiu was strict, so the *friendly* nod he gave me on my first morning in the word-herb hall surprised me. He pointed to an empty stool beside him without a word, and I understood I was welcome. We worked side by side through the morning bell and the noon bell, and by evening I had learned more from watching his hands than from any scroll. Behind us, Xiaoxing smiled as if she had arranged it.
friendly:2.cnHint: 我原以为师兄性格严厉，但他对我____的点头让我受宠若惊，两人就此并肩学习。
friendly:2.hook: That night Xiaoxing's candle burned in a shape no wind could explain.
friendly:2.line: 'A *friendly* hall is a learning hall — sit down, we have much to copy today.'

sentences.en: I had heard Shen Wujiu was strict, so the *friendly* nod he gave me on my first morning in the word-herb hall surprised me.
He pointed to an empty stool beside him without a word, and I understood I was welcome.
sentences.cn: 他没说话就指了指身边的空凳子，我明白了我是受欢迎的。

sentences.en: We worked side by side through the morning bell and the noon bell, and by evening I had learned more from watching his hands than from any scroll.
sentences.cn: 整个上午我们并肩工作，从晨钟到午钟，到了傍晚，我从看他的手学到的东西比读过的任何卷轴都多。

sentences.en: Behind us, Xiaoxing smiled as if she had arranged it.
sentences.cn: 小杏在我们身后笑着，好像这一切都是她安排的。

indeed:2.en: The sealed jar on my desk had not moved in three days. When I finally opened it, the herb inside had *indeed* taken the shape of a tiny cloud, just as the old text promised. Xiaoxing leaned close and whispered that she had never seen a herb respond so quickly to a new disciple.
indeed:2.cnHint: 打开封存的药罐，里面的灵草____如古籍所述，化作了云的形状。
indeed:2.hook: But the cloud shape was slowly turning the colour of ash.
indeed:2.line: 'It has *indeed* grown into the form the old masters described.'

sentences.en: The sealed jar on my desk had not moved in three days.
sentences.cn: 我桌上的那只密封罐三天没动过。

sentences.en: When I finally opened it, the herb inside had *indeed* taken the shape of a tiny cloud, just as the old text promised.
Xiaoxing leaned close and whispered that she had never seen a herb respond so quickly to a new disciple.
sentences.cn: 小杏凑近了，小声说她从没见过一株草对新弟子反应这么快。

launch:2.en: At the edge of the eastern cliff, Shen Wujiu showed me the brass tube carved with wind-words. He pressed three characters in order, and the small paper vessel inside rose with a clean, sharp *launch*, carrying our message straight up through the clouds toward Master Qingwu's peak above.
launch:2.cnHint: 师兄演示了铜管传讯之法，信笺在一次干净的____中飞向师尊所在的山峰。
launch:2.hook: The paper vessel did not come back down.
launch:2.line: 'Watch the angle before you attempt the *launch* — one wrong word and it folds.'

sentences.en: At the edge of the eastern cliff, Shen Wujiu showed me the brass tube carved with wind-words.
sentences.cn: 在东悬崖边，沈无咎给我看了那根刻着风字的铜管。

sentences.en: He pressed three characters in order, and the small paper vessel inside rose with a clean, sharp *launch*, carrying our message straight up through the clouds toward Master Qingwu's peak above.

refer:2.en: Xiaoxing pressed a folded page into my hand outside the herb hall. She told me to *refer* to the third column whenever a spiritual character refused to stay lit on the page, because Master Qingwu had written a correction there that the main copy did not carry.
refer:2.cnHint: 师妹交给我一张笔记，告诉我遇到灵字熄灭时，要去____其中的第三列。
refer:2.hook: The third column had been crossed out in red ink I did not recognise.
refer:2.line: 'Please *refer* to that column before you try the night formula alone.'

sentences.en: Xiaoxing pressed a folded page into my hand outside the herb hall.
sentences.cn: 小杏在草药堂外把一张折好的纸塞进我手里。

sentences.en: She told me to *refer* to the third column whenever a spiritual character refused to stay lit on the page, because Master Qingwu had written a correction there that the main copy did not carry.

trust:2.en: Master Qingwu set a small jade slip on the stone table between us. She said the sect placed its full *trust* in those chosen to carry the slip, because the characters sealed inside could open the cloud gate from any mountain if spoken correctly, and that responsibility was not light.
trust:2.cnHint: 师尊将玉简置于桌上，说持有它的人肩负着门派全部的____。
trust:2.hook: A thin crack ran along the jade I had not seen a moment before.
trust:2.line: 'The slip is given only where *trust* has been earned, not assumed.'

sentences.en: Master Qingwu set a small jade slip on the stone table between us.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊在石桌中间放了一块小玉片。

sentences.en: She said the sect placed its full *trust* in those chosen to carry the slip, because the characters sealed inside could open the cloud gate from any mountain if spoken correctly, and that responsibility was not light.

discussion:2.en: I found a record of an old *discussion* pressed between two stone slabs near the library cave. Three masters had written their thoughts about whether words of flight could ever be truly safe for first-year disciples, and none of the three had reached the same answer.
discussion:2.cnHint: 我在藏经洞附近发现了一份古老的____记录，三位前辈对飞行字诀各持不同看法。
discussion:2.hook: The final line of the record had been torn cleanly away.
discussion:2.line: 'That *discussion* was never finished — no one agreed, and then the storm came.'

sentences.en: I found a record of an old *discussion* pressed between two stone slabs near the library cave.
Three masters had written their thoughts about whether words of flight could ever be truly safe for first-year disciples, and none of the three had reached the same answer.
sentences.cn: 三位师尊写了他们对"飞行的字"是否真的对一年级弟子安全的看法，但三个人谁也没得出同样的结论。

extremely:2.en: Shen Wujiu found me studying the wall chart and pointed to the red-bordered row near the bottom. He said those word-combinations were *extremely* rare and that most disciples spent ten years without seeing even one appear naturally in a herb, so I should record the exact shape before it faded.
extremely:2.cnHint: 师兄指着图表下方提醒我，那类字符组合____罕见，要赶快记录下来。
extremely:2.hook: When I turned back to the herb, the shape had already changed.
extremely:2.line: 'Be careful — that reaction is *extremely* rare and it will not hold long.'

sentences.en: Shen Wujiu found me studying the wall chart and pointed to the red-bordered row near the bottom.
sentences.cn: 沈无咎看到我在研究墙上的图表，指了指底部靠近边框的那一行。

sentences.en: He said those word-combinations were *extremely* rare and that most disciples spent ten years without seeing even one appear naturally in a herb, so I should record the exact shape before it faded.

organize:2.en: Before the night trial, Master Qingwu asked me to *organize* the word-slips by the season they were gathered, not by the mountain. It took me two hours, and when I laid the last slip down, the whole arrangement glowed faintly, as if the order itself had pleased something sleeping beneath the stones.
organize:2.cnHint: 师尊让我按采集季节____玉简，排列完成后，整组玉简发出了微弱的光芒。
organize:2.hook: The glow pulsed once, then sank into the floor without a sound.
organize:2.line: '*Organize* them by season first — the mountain order comes later, if at all.'

sentences.en: Before the night trial, Master Qingwu asked me to *organize* the word-slips by the season they were gathered, not by the mountain.
It took me two hours, and when I laid the last slip down, the whole arrangement glowed faintly, as if the order itself had pleased something sleeping beneath the stones.
sentences.cn: 花了我两个小时，当我放下最后一块字片时，整个排列都隐隐发光，好像这个顺序本身愉悦了什么沉睡在石头下面的东西。

pattern:2.en: Xiaoxing had been watching the clouds below our mountain for seven mornings. She showed me her notes and traced a slow *pattern* in the mist — the same spiral, always beginning at dawn, always dissolving before the second bell. She believed a word was forming down there, enormous and old.
pattern:2.cnHint: 师妹连续七天观察云海，发现云雾中有一个反复出现的____，像是某个巨大而古老的字。
pattern:2.hook: That morning the spiral did not dissolve — it held, and began to rise.
pattern:2.line: 'Look closely — this *pattern* has repeated every dawn since the rains stopped.'

sentences.en: Xiaoxing had been watching the clouds below our mountain for seven mornings.
sentences.cn: 小杏已经连续七个清晨都在看着我们山下的云。

sentences.en: She showed me her notes and traced a slow *pattern* in the mist — the same spiral, always beginning at dawn, always dissolving before the second bell.
She believed a word was forming down there, enormous and old.
sentences.cn: 她相信有一个词正在下面形成，巨大而古老。

transform:2.en: The old storage cave smelled of pine smoke and forgotten years. I found a scroll buried beneath three layers of silk — its ink still bright, alive. Master Qingwu had written that a single mastered word could *transform* raw mountain mist into a shield of breath. I read it once, and felt the air around my hands thicken.
transform:2.cnHint: 我在储藏洞中发现了一卷古老的卷轴，记载着一个词能____周围的山雾。
transform:2.hook: Then the scroll began to fold itself closed.
transform:2.line: 'One true word can *transform* the world around you,' Master Qingwu had written.

sentences.en: The old storage cave smelled of pine smoke and forgotten years.
sentences.cn: 那间古老的储藏洞闻起来像松烟和被遗忘的岁月。

sentences.en: I found a scroll buried beneath three layers of silk — its ink still bright, alive.
sentences.cn: 我在三层丝绸下面找到了一卷经文——墨迹依旧鲜活闪亮。

sentences.en: Master Qingwu had written that a single mastered word could *transform* raw mountain mist into a shield of breath.
I read it once, and felt the air around my hands thicken.
sentences.cn: 我读了一遍，感觉手周围的空气变得厚重了。

additional:2.en: Shen Wujiu spread the supply records across the stone table. Each disciple was given five basic words per season. But tucked inside my name's row was a small mark — a circle in red ink. It meant *additional* instruction: a sixth word, granted to very few. I did not know whether to feel honoured or afraid.
additional:2.cnHint: 师兄展示了弟子名册，我的名字旁有个红圈，标注了____的功课。
additional:2.hook: No one had received that mark in seven years.
additional:2.line: 'You have been given *additional* words — do not waste them,' Shen Wujiu said quietly.

sentences.en: Shen Wujiu spread the supply records across the stone table.
sentences.cn: 沈无咎把补给记录铺开在石桌上。

sentences.en: Each disciple was given five basic words per season.
sentences.cn: 每个弟子每个季节只能得到五个基础之词。

sentences.en: But tucked inside my name's row was a small mark — a circle in red ink.
sentences.cn: 但夹在我名字那一行里有个小记号——用红墨水画的一个圆圈。

sentences.en: It meant *additional* instruction: a sixth word, granted to very few.
I did not know whether to feel honoured or afraid.
sentences.cn: 我不知道该感到荣幸还是害怕。

journal:2.en: Behind the medicine shelf, wedged between two clay jars, I found a thin book with no name on its cover. It was a *journal* — daily entries in a hand I did not know, each page recording one word learned and one wound healed. The last entry was dated the morning of the last great storm. After that, the pages were blank.
journal:2.cnHint: 药架后面藏着一本无名____，记录着每天学到的词与治好的伤。
journal:2.hook: A pressed cloud-flower fell from between the final pages.
journal:2.line: 'A *journal* holds what memory drops,' Xiaoxing whispered, touching the cover.

sentences.en: Behind the medicine shelf, wedged between two clay jars, I found a thin book with no name on its cover.
sentences.cn: 在药架后面，夹在两个陶罐之间，我找到了一本没有封面名字的薄书。

sentences.en: It was a *journal* — daily entries in a hand I did not know, each page recording one word learned and one wound healed.
The last entry was dated the morning of the last great storm.
sentences.cn: 最后一条记录的日期是上一场大风暴的那个清晨。

sentences.en: After that, the pages were blank.
sentences.cn: 之后，页面都空白了。

sort:2.en: The word-seeds in the sect's archive were kept in rows of small wooden drawers. Xiaoxing showed me how to *sort* them — not by shape or colour, but by the feeling they left on the tongue when you spoke them silently. Healing words were warm. Words for flight tasted of cold wind. I sorted seven before my hands began to tremble.
sort:2.cnHint: 师妹教我如何用舌尖的感觉来____词种，而不是按颜色或形状。
sort:2.hook: The eighth word burned before I could place it.
sort:2.line: '*Sort* by feeling first — your tongue knows before your mind does,' Xiaoxing said.

sentences.en: The word-seeds in the sect's archive were kept in rows of small wooden drawers.
sentences.cn: 宗派档案库里的词种子被放在一排排小木抽屉里。

sentences.en: Xiaoxing showed me how to *sort* them — not by shape or colour, but by the feeling they left on the tongue when you spoke them silently.
Healing words were warm.
sentences.cn: 治疗之词是温暖的。

sentences.en: Words for flight tasted of cold wind.
sentences.cn: 飞行之词尝起来像冷风。

sentences.en: I sorted seven before my hands began to tremble.
sentences.cn: 我分类了七个后，手开始发抖。

understanding:2.en: I had copied the formula for cloud-walking twelve times, yet my feet still refused to leave the stone path. Master Qingwu watched without speaking. At last she said that copying was not enough — that true *understanding* lived below words, in the body's quiet agreement with them. I closed my eyes, stopped trying to remember, and felt the path soften.
understanding:2.cnHint: 我抄写了十二遍飞云口诀，师尊说真正的____不在于记忆，而在于身体的感受。
understanding:2.hook: A single foot lifted, just slightly, off the stone.
understanding:2.line: 'Memorising words and *understanding* them are two very different paths,' said Master Qingwu.

sentences.en: I had copied the formula for cloud-walking twelve times, yet my feet still refused to leave the stone path.
sentences.cn: 我已经抄了十二遍踏云的公式，可我的脚还是拒绝离开石路。

sentences.en: Master Qingwu watched without speaking.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊默默地看着。

sentences.en: At last she said that copying was not enough — that true *understanding* lived below words, in the body's quiet agreement with them.
I closed my eyes, stopped trying to remember, and felt the path soften.
sentences.cn: 我闭上眼睛，停止努力去记忆，感觉路面变软了。

citizen:2.en: The archive listed every person who had ever studied at the Cloud Sea Sect — disciple, elder, visitor. One column used the word *citizen*, marking those who came not from mountain families but from the lowland towns far below the clouds. My name carried that mark. I had not known the sect kept such records, or that my origin had already been noted.
citizen:2.cnHint: 档案中用____一词标注了来自云下平原城镇的弟子，我的名字旁就有这个标记。
citizen:2.hook: Someone had circled my entry in fresh ink.
citizen:2.line: 'A *citizen* of the low towns can still master the highest word,' Shen Wujiu said firmly.

sentences.en: The archive listed every person who had ever studied at the Cloud Sea Sect — disciple, elder, visitor.
sentences.cn: 档案列了每一个曾在云海宗学过的人——弟子、长老、访客。

sentences.en: One column used the word *citizen*, marking those who came not from mountain families but from the lowland towns far below the clouds.
My name carried that mark.
sentences.cn: 我的名字带着那个标记。

sentences.en: I had not known the sect kept such records, or that my origin had already been noted.
sentences.cn: 我不知道宗派保留这样的记录，也不知道我的出身已经被记下来了。

contrast:2.en: Two practice slates hung side by side on the archive wall — one carved by a senior disciple of twenty years, one by a student on their first day. Master Qingwu asked me to study the *contrast*: not to feel shame, but to measure the distance between a beginning and a mastery worth aiming for. I looked for a long time, then picked up my own brush.
contrast:2.cnHint: 两块习字石板并排挂着，师尊让我观察其____，不是为了羞愧，而是为了找到方向。
contrast:2.hook: My reflection appeared in the polished surface of the older slate.
contrast:2.line: 'Study the *contrast*, and let it show you where to walk next,' said Master Qingwu.

sentences.en: Two practice slates hung side by side on the archive wall — one carved by a senior disciple of twenty years, one by a student on their first day.
sentences.cn: 两块练习石板并排挂在档案库的墙上——一块是二十年资历的高级弟子刻的，一块是学生在第一天刻的。

sentences.en: Master Qingwu asked me to study the *contrast*: not to feel shame, but to measure the distance between a beginning and a mastery worth aiming for.
I looked for a long time, then picked up my own brush.
sentences.cn: 我看了很久，然后拿起了我自己的笔。

establish:2.en: In the lowest chamber of the archive, a flat stone bore the founding words of the Cloud Sea Sect — the first four formulas spoken to *establish* this place above the clouds, to anchor a floating mountain and make it home. The characters were worn but still warm to the touch. I pressed my palm against them and felt something press back.
establish:2.cnHint: 档案室最底层的石碑上刻着最初用来____云海宗的四个词诀。
establish:2.hook: A low hum rose from the stone, as if it recognised my hand.
establish:2.line: 'Those words were spoken to *establish* a home where none could exist,' Shen Wujiu said softly.

sentences.en: In the lowest chamber of the archive, a flat stone bore the founding words of the Cloud Sea Sect — the first four formulas spoken to *establish* this place above the clouds, to anchor a floating mountain and make it home.
The characters were worn but still warm to the touch.
sentences.cn: 字迹磨损了，但仍然热得烫手。

sentences.en: I pressed my palm against them and felt something press back.
sentences.cn: 我把手掌按在上面，感觉有什么东西按了回来。

security:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and quiet ink. Master Qingwu had sealed every window with a word-formula, each character glowing faintly gold. 'This room is our *security*,' she said, pressing a warm hand to my shoulder. Outside, the wind had begun to carry something strange — a low hum that did not belong to any herb we had learned.
security:0.cnHint: 师尊用字符封住了内堂的每扇窗，说这里是我们的____，而窗外的风声开始变得异常。
security:0.hook: The sealed characters flickered once, then went dark.
security:0.line: 'This room is our *security* — do not open the windows tonight.'

sentences.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and quiet ink.
sentences.cn: 内堂里弥漫着陈年松木和静谧墨香的气息。

sentences.en: Master Qingwu had sealed every window with a word-formula, each character glowing faintly gold.
sentences.cn: 青梧师尊用符咒封了每一扇窗，每个字都闪烁着淡淡的金光。

sentences.en: 'This room is our *security*,' she said, pressing a warm hand to my shoulder.
Outside, the wind had begun to carry something strange — a low hum that did not belong to any herb we had learned.
sentences.cn: 外面的风开始吹来奇怪的东西——一种低沉的嗡鸣声，不属于我们学过的任何草药。
